what_it_does: This paper addresses the memory wall problem where applications spend most time waiting for data instead of computing. Some chips include near-memory processing (NMP) units—simpler processors located next to memory—that can compute on data before it travels to the main processor, saving bandwidth and energy. However, identifying which computations benefit from offloading to NMP units is difficult because applications have varying memory access characteristics, and existing methods require massive labeled training datasets. The paper proposes an unsupervised clustering approach that automatically identifies which parts of an application are memory-intensive without human annotation, targeting only those regions for offloading to NMP.
